title: Is thirty eight a perfect square, by taking away odd numbers?
description: The video takes odd numbers away from thirty eight, starting at one, to decide if it is a perfect square. Keeko doubts the answer after taking away six odd numbers and calling thirty eight six squared.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number is a perfect square only if taking away odd numbers from one lands exactly on zero. Watch for students who stop when the leftover is small and treat it as close enough.

source: Use successive subtraction of odd numbers to decide whether 38 is a perfect square.
video_script.why: The child learns to test a number by subtracting odd numbers from one, and to read the result: exactly zero means a perfect square, and going below zero means it is not.
video_script.substitution: Subtract 1, 3, 5 and so on from the number, and see if the leftover lands exactly on zero.
video_script.anchor: the number thirty eight with the odd numbers one, three, five and so on lined up beside it
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes away six odd numbers, sees only two left, and says thirty eight is six squared. Six squared is thirty six, and the leftover must be exactly zero.
video_script.payoff_line: Thirty eight is not a perfect square

final_answer.spoken: thirty eight is not a perfect square

never_show: the square root of 81 by subtraction
maths_rules: the next odd number is 13 and 2 − 13 = −11, which is below 0; we never land on 0
check: 6² = 36 and 7² = 49, and 38 lies between them
the slip: 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 + 11 = 36 = 6², not 38; the leftover is 2
video_script.design: One idea: land exactly on zero, or it is not a perfect square. Wrong idea: a small leftover is close enough. The number stays in the anchor band and the leftovers drop down the working board.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to decide if thirty eight is a perfect square.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, take away one, three and five. Thirty eight minus one is thirty seven.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Thirty seven minus three is thirty four, and the leftover keeps getting smaller.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Thirty four minus five is twenty nine, and the next odd number is seven.

marks.eleven: 13 − 11 = 2 is written and the 2 is ringed

narration: <bookmark mark='seven'/>Step two, take away seven, nine and eleven. Twenty nine minus seven is twenty two.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>Twenty two minus nine is thirteen, and the odd numbers are still going up.
<bookmark mark='eleven'/>Thirteen minus eleven leaves two, which is not zero.

narration: <bookmark mark='next'/>Step three, the next odd number is thirteen.
<bookmark mark='below'/>Two minus thirteen goes below zero. We never landed on zero.

marks.check: 38 is placed between 36 and 49 on a number line

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check with the squares around it. Six squared is thirty six and seven squared is forty nine, and thirty eight lies between them.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 38 is not a perfect square
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Thirty eight is not a perfect square.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks thirty eight is six squared, because six odd numbers were taken away.
<bookmark mark='six'/>But six squared is thirty six, and two was left over.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The leftover must be exactly zero, so close is not enough.
